newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - June 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - June 18.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Wednesday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY
- The foreign affairs department and numerous major companies have signed up with callback operators, threatening to erode Telkom's revenue from international calls.

- In a concession to organised agriculture, Land Affairs Minister Derek Hanekom has softened key clauses in a controversial bill which aims to give tenure security to hundreds of thousands of farm workers.
- Gencor Ltd was poised to lift its share of world nickel production significantly through a partnership deal with Australian producer Queensland Nickel (QNI) Ltd, analysts said on Tuesday.
- A proposal by three southern African states to reopen world trade in ivory was defeated by three votes at the Convention for International Trade in Endangered Species (CITES) meeting on Tuesday.

- The South African Medical and Dental Council, which came under fire for its passive role in the death of activist Steve Biko in detention in 1977, admitted on Tuesday it could have done more in treating detainees.
BUSINESS REPORT

- Foreign banks operating in South Africa expected employment in their ranks to rise by 73 percent in the next five years, creating nearly 800 new jobs, according to a survey released on Tuesday by accounting firm Price Waterhouse.

- Negotiations on the controversial employment standards bill were pointless, an the proposed law should go straight to parliament where organised labour was confident of getting its way, Sam Shilowa, Cosatu general secretary, said on Tuesday.
- Abe and Solly Krok, the pharmaceutical magnates, have lodged an application for a casino licence at Gold Reef City, the entertainment complex in the corridor between Johannesburg and Soweto.

- Mine-level negotiations between JCI Ltd's Randfontein Estates Gold Mine Ltd and the National Union of Mineworkers over the fate of thousands of workers facing retrenchment ended without agreement on Tuesday, Marc Gonsalves, a company spokesman, said.
SAKE BEELD

- The possibility of a second nationwide strike over the draft bill on employment standards is growing stronger following the call by the trade union federation Cosatu that Nedlac negotiations should be suspended to allow parliament to settle the dispute.
- Investments under the management of Investec's foreign partner Insinger now amounts to $12 billion (54 billion rand).
- The government on Tuesday announced a wide-ranging campaign to stamp out corruption, fraud and theft from the public service.
THE STAR

- Spurred on by the culture of lawlessness on Johannesburg's roads and the absence of visible law enforcement, the city's motorists have not bothered to pay two-thirds of about 700,000 traffic fines issued over the past year.

- A Ventersdorp petrol attendant assaulted by Afrikaner Weerstandsbeweging (AWB) leader Eugene TerreBlanche, who received an effective six-year jail term on Tuesday for committing serious assault and attempted murder, says he still lives in fear.

- A Cleveland police constable accused of murdering a 28-year-old Newlands, Johannesburg, man by shooting him in the charge office six times, was arrested for murder in 1995 but the case was withdrawn after state witnesses failed to appear in court, the Johannesburg District Court has heard.

- The Representative Association of Medical Schemes (RAMS), an umbrella body representing medical aid schemes across the country, said on Tuesday it would not accept or approve any increase in the cost of medicines in spite of pharmacies' threats to boycott medical aid members unless they paid cash for their prescribed medicine.
